verifiedBehavior.boundedChildLifecycle: managed probe/analysis/ocr/render commands implement a bounded child lifecycle using process-group-capable detached spawning; termination begins with SIGTERM, escalates to SIGKILL, with bounded TERM grace and post-KILL settle
verifiedBehavior.detachedProcessGroupSignal: on Linux the runner signals the entire process group (processImpl.kill(-pid, signal)) so descendants share the leader's lifecycle
verifiedBehavior.forcedSettle: a child that never emits close (or an overflow/timeout path) is forced through TERM-to-KILL then a bounded forced settle so no managed child is left alive
verifiedBehavior.descendantAndLeaderGone: the group-escape fixture proves via direct live-poll assertions that both the SIGTERM-ignoring descendant PID is reaped AND the leader process group is gone after escalation
verifiedBehavior.boundedStdoutStderr: stdout is capped (text and binary stdout caps); stderr is capped to a tail; managed errors expose only bounded stderr-size diagnostics
verifiedBehavior.noRawStderrLeakage: managed errors carry a bounded stderrTailBytes and no raw stderr payload (no raw this.stderrTail assignment)
verifiedBehavior.abortCancellation: managed runners accept a caller AbortSignal, addEventListener('abort'), re-check after consumer spawn, and terminate the active child on cancellation (process_cancelled); external-signal and reentrant-abort fixtures prove cancellation on a real child
verifiedBehavior.shutdownCancellation: abortAllManagedProcesses('shutdown') requests cancellation of every active managed process and the MANAGED_PROCESS_SHUTDOWN_REQUESTED latch rejects any later subprocess stage before it spawns
verifiedBehavior.synchronousRealChildEvidence: runner tests capture a real child pid synchronously in the spawn seam (capture.pid = child.pid) and gate readiness on the actual readyFile marker via an awaited bounded waitForFileSync before the production timer starts, so PID/readiness evidence is real and deterministically ordered before the deadline
verifiedBehavior.ownedTempCleanupPreservingSiblings: both production cleanup paths route their per-row teardown through the shared removeOwnedWorkdir(workingDir) seam on the exact local workingDir, never a parent path, preserving an unrelated sibling sentinel
